verdicts.rationale: The introduction identifies an existing predictor and potentially prohibitive joint retraining lasting weeks or months as the practical motivation.
The predictor is trained first using a classification surrogate; the second stage learns deferral with the predictor-derived score fixed.
Equation (3) weights the predictor option by its correctness indicator and expert options by complementary deferral costs.
The experiments section names both datasets and precisely these predictor, deferral and expert architectures.
The reported training setup matches the losses, optimizer, batch size, weight decay, dataset-specific epochs and absence of augmentation.
The contributions explicitly describe both surrogate families and their H-consistency bounds implying Bayes-consistency.
Theorems 1 and 6 impose the respective stage-specific consistency-bound assumptions and retain minimizability gaps in the deferral bounds.
Theorems 5 and 7 state zero expected deferral loss for the specified minimizers under logistic losses, constant costs, scaling closure and realizability.
The fixed-score multiclass result is identified as a contribution, and Theorem 3 assumes symmetry and completeness of the underlying class.
All six values and the three-run mean and standard deviation reporting match Table 4; the methods identify its first two rows as lacking base costs.
All six values and uncertainty summaries match Table 4; the methods identify its last two rows as using base costs.
The authors explicitly report being unaware of established baselines within this setting.
The limitation paragraph states that costs are typically determined through cross-validation and reserves principled selection for future research.
